nodes.name: Incoming connector
nodes.description: Receives data from a node of ANOTHER automation — the door through which this automation joins a group. It is an OFFER, not a dependency: kept hidden, the automation runs perfectly well on its own.

info.aiSummary: Waits for data from a neighbouring automation; in a standalone automation it stays hidden.

function.name: receiveFromExternal
function.summary: Takes the payload handed over by another automation and names it for this one.
function.accepts: The payload as another automation handed it over.
function.returns: payload — the same value, named for this automation.

nodes.name: Control panel input
nodes.description: The default door: the owner's message typed into the control panel form.

info.aiSummary: Captures the control-panel form message (the default channel when a run names no source) and normalizes it into the shared Message. An empty message is refused at the door in ten languages; a run of another channel is passed through untouched.

function.name: receiveControlPanel
function.summary: Captures the control-panel form message and normalizes it into the shared Message shape.
function.accepts: The form fields of a run started from the control panel: text (required), optional lat/lng.
function.returns: Message fields merged into the context: text, source="control-panel", at, and lat/lng when given.

nodes.name: Webhook input
nodes.description: An external system calls in over HTTP.

info.aiSummary: Captures an HTTP push (POST api/run with source="webhook") and normalizes its JSON body into the shared Message: text ← text/message/payload, a structured payload is serialized rather than lost. Empty body — refused at the door. Input is push-only: nothing is polled.

function.name: receiveWebhook
function.summary: Normalizes an external HTTP push into the shared Message; a structured payload is serialized, never lost.
function.accepts: The JSON body of POST api/run with source="webhook": text, message or payload, optional lat/lng.
function.returns: Message fields merged into the context: text, source="webhook", at, and lat/lng when given.

nodes.name: Cron input
nodes.description: A scheduled tick fires it on a timer.

info.aiSummary: Turns a scheduler tick (POST api/run with source="cron") into a synthetic Message — the tick's own text or "Scheduled tick at <time>". The schedule itself is declared in the folder's cron.json when the owner enables the channel; the tick is a push, not a poll.

function.name: receiveCron
function.summary: Turns a scheduled tick into a synthetic Message so downstream work is exercised on a timer.
function.accepts: The tick pushed by the scheduler: optional text/message; nothing else is required.
function.returns: Message fields merged into the context: text (given or synthetic), source="cron", at.

nodes.name: Public Page input
nodes.description: A form or control on the automation own public page.

info.aiSummary: Captures a visitor's message from the automation's public page form (POST api/run with source="public-page") and normalizes it into the shared Message. Same normalization as the control panel; a separate channel so outputs can tell visitors from the owner.

function.name: receivePublicPage
function.summary: Captures a visitor's message from the public page form and normalizes it into the shared Message.
function.accepts: The form fields of a run with source="public-page": text (required), optional lat/lng.
function.returns: Message fields merged into the context: text, source="public-page", at, and lat/lng when given.

nodes.name: Telegram Bot input
nodes.description: A message sent to the automation own Telegram bot.

info.aiSummary: Captures a message sent to the automation's own Telegram bot: the listener pushes the update into api/run with source="telegram-bot", and the node understands both the raw Telegram shape ({message:{text,chat}}) and a pre-parsed text. The sender's chat id is kept in the context so a reply can reach exactly them. Live intake is gated on the channel keys.

envKeys.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

envKeys.name: TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_CHAT_ID
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

function.name: receiveTelegramBot
function.summary: Normalizes a Telegram-bot update into the shared Message and keeps the sender's chat id for replies.
function.accepts: A pushed update with source="telegram-bot": raw {message:{text,chat:{id}}} or pre-parsed text.
function.returns: Message fields (text, source="telegram-bot", at) plus telegramChatId when the update names the chat.

nodes.name: User Telegram Chat input
nodes.description: A message read from the user own Telegram chat.

info.aiSummary: Captures a message from the user's own Telegram chat (linked natively via api/telegram/link): the listener pushes it into api/run with source="user-telegram-chat". Differs from telegram-bot by WHO writes — the user in their personal chat, not outsiders writing to the automation's bot. Live intake is gated on the channel keys.

envKeys.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

function.name: receiveUserTelegramChat
function.summary: Normalizes a message from the user's own linked Telegram chat into the shared Message.
function.accepts: A pushed update with source="user-telegram-chat": raw Telegram shape or pre-parsed text.
function.returns: Message fields (text, source="user-telegram-chat", at) plus telegramChatId when named.

nodes.name: Email input
nodes.description: Input for an email delivered to the automation's intake address.

info.aiSummary: Captures an inbound email: the provider pushes it into the api/inbound-email door (signature-checked), which starts a run with source="email". The body (or the subject when the body is empty) becomes the Message text; sender and subject stay in the context so the email output can reply to the sender. No mailbox polling — input is push-only.

envKeys.name: RESEND_API_KEY
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

envKeys.name: RESEND_FROM_EMAIL
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

envKeys.name: RESEND_INBOUND_SECRET
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

function.name: receiveEmail
function.summary: Normalizes an inbound email into the shared Message; sender and subject stay available for a reply.
function.accepts: The parsed letter pushed by api/inbound-email: from (required), subject, text.
function.returns: Message fields (text, source="email", at) plus emailFrom and emailSubject.

nodes.name: Logic
nodes.description: The middle — the deterministic work that turns the input into the output.

info.aiSummary: Validates and normalizes the captured Message: non-empty text (an empty capture fails the run in ten languages), collapsed whitespace, a title derived from the first line, stamped at/source. Deterministic, no keys, no AI — this throw is the real success/failure gate of the flow.

function.name: transformPayload
function.summary: Validates the captured message and derives its title; an empty capture honestly fails the run.
function.accepts: The Message fields put into the context by the input node of the run's channel.
function.returns: text · title · at · source — the normalized message every output node consumes.

outcomes.name: normalized
outcomes.when: the capture carried text
outcomes.puts: text · title · at · source — the normalized message

outcomes.name: empty
outcomes.when: the capture carried no text
outcomes.puts: nothing: the run fails honestly at this gate

nodes.name: If success
nodes.description: The branch taken when the middle produced a result — the flow continues to the output.

info.aiSummary: The success branch: holds only when the normalized message carries non-empty text — then the flow fans out to every open output. When it does not hold, the node returns null and the run stops lawfully (the middle's throw is the loud failure; this is the quiet gate).

function.name: ifSuccess
function.summary: Lets the flow through to the outputs only when a non-empty normalized message exists.
function.accepts: The normalized message (text · title · at · source) produced by the middle.
function.returns: The same context when the branch holds; null (a lawful stop) when it does not.

outcomes.name: holding
outcomes.when: the run carries a payload and no node declared a refusal
outcomes.puts: the flow continues to the delivery doors

outcomes.name: not-holding
outcomes.when: a node declared a refusal (an unreachable source, a failed download)
outcomes.puts: the branch does not hold — the failure branch carries the reason

outcomes.name: nothing-to-deliver
outcomes.when: the middle found nothing to store
outcomes.puts: the branch does not hold: there is no result to deliver

nodes.name: If failure
nodes.description: The branch taken when the middle could not produce a result — the flow ends here.

info.aiSummary: The failure branch: a named dead end on the canvas. The real failure has already stopped the run with the middle's throw (empty capture, refused input), so the function is an honest no-op — the node exists so the owner SEES where a failed run ends.

function.name: ifFailure
function.summary: Ends the flow when the middle produced no message; the canvas shows where a failed run stops.
function.accepts: The failure reported by the middle of the flow.
function.returns: Nothing — a failure branch ends the flow.

outcomes.name: failed
outcomes.when: a node declared a refusal and named its reason
outcomes.puts: the reason travels to the toast, so the human learns what happened

outcomes.name: empty-handed
outcomes.when: the run produced nothing to store
outcomes.puts: the toast says so plainly

outcomes.name: not-holding
outcomes.when: the run succeeded — this branch is not its path
outcomes.puts: nothing

nodes.name: Fetch the subject
nodes.description: Brings the named subject from an open encyclopedic source: description, image address, coordinates. The subject is named by the human at run time — this node does not know what it is.

info.aiSummary: Brings the named subject from an open encyclopedic source: description, image address, coordinates. The subject is named by the human at run time — this node does not know what it is.

function.name: fetchExternal
function.summary: Fetches the named subject from an open, keyless encyclopedic source.
function.accepts: The subject name the human wrote (ctx.text), for the classes fetch-external and composite.
function.returns: subject (name · description · imageUrl · lat/lng · sourceUrl) plus text/title/coordinates in the message contract — or subjectMissing / subjectError, honestly.

outcomes.name: found
outcomes.when: the source answered and carried a description
outcomes.puts: subject (name · description · image · coordinates) plus the message contract

outcomes.name: missing
outcomes.when: the source answered but knows nothing about the named subject
outcomes.puts: subjectMissing plus skipStores — nothing is written

outcomes.name: unreachable
outcomes.when: the source refused or the network failed (e.g. HTTP 403)
outcomes.puts: subjectError plus skipStores — the failure is named, never mistaken for “nothing found”

outcomes.name: not-mine
outcomes.when: the run belongs to another request class
outcomes.puts: nothing: the flow passes through untouched

nodes.name: Keep the object
nodes.description: Downloads the bytes of the subject's image and keeps them in the folder's object storage, so a record can point at an object of ours rather than at somebody else's link.

info.aiSummary: Downloads the bytes of the subject's image and keeps them in the folder's object storage, so a record can point at an object of ours rather than at somebody else's link.

function.name: keepObject
function.summary: Downloads the subject image and keeps it in the folder object storage.
function.accepts: ctx.subject with an imageUrl.
function.returns: attachments[] with the stored fileKey — or objectError; a subject without an image is a lawful silence.

outcomes.name: kept
outcomes.when: the image was downloaded into the folder object storage
outcomes.puts: attachments[] with the stored fileKey

outcomes.name: nothing-to-keep
outcomes.when: the subject carries no image
outcomes.puts: nothing: a subject without a picture is still a subject

outcomes.name: unreachable
outcomes.when: the image address refused or the file was too large
outcomes.puts: objectError — named, not silent

nodes.name: Resolve the moment
nodes.description: Finds the date bound to the subject in its own description and puts it into ctx.when, so the calendar can place an event by the ordinary path. Deterministic: a parsed year, never a guessed date.

info.aiSummary: Finds the date bound to the subject in its own description and puts it into ctx.when, so the calendar can place an event by the ordinary path. Deterministic: a parsed year, never a guessed date.

function.name: resolveMoment
function.summary: Extracts the moment bound to the subject and puts it into ctx.when.
function.accepts: ctx.subject with a description.
function.returns: when (ISO) plus momentPrecision/momentSource — or nothing, when the description carries no date.

outcomes.name: dated
outcomes.when: a plausible year was found in the subject description
outcomes.puts: when (ISO) plus momentPrecision

outcomes.name: undated
outcomes.when: the description carries no date
outcomes.puts: nothing: the calendar simply does not fire

nodes.name: Toast output
nodes.description: The one channel that always carries the run outcome — success and failure alike. It cannot be hidden: an automation able to fail silently is exactly what this law removes.

info.aiSummary: Writes the run outcome and its reason where the human can see it: a row of the toast table plus the run journal. Accepts BOTH branches. Never pretends to be a delivery into somebody else's channel — for a run that came from a bot the last word still belongs to that channel.

function.name: deliverToast
function.summary: Writes the run outcome and its reason where the human can see it.
function.accepts: The outcome named by the last validator plus whatever reason the nodes left in the context.
function.returns: toastRowId · toastOutcome.

nodes.name: Dashboard output
nodes.description: A row in the automation dashboard's history table.

info.aiSummary: Writes the captured message into the dashboard history table: one row per successful run — date · source · title · text (folder-local rows store, _lib/rows.ts).

function.name: deliverDashboard
function.summary: Writes one history row per successful run: date, source channel, title and text of the message.
function.accepts: The normalized message (text · title · at · source) carried by the success branch.
function.returns: rowId — the id of the history row written to the dashboard.

nodes.name: Outgoing connector
nodes.description: Hands the result over to a node of ANOTHER automation — the door out into a group.

info.aiSummary: Passes the WHOLE shared Message to a neighbouring automation — the far side receives the same contract every channel speaks. Provable only inside a group of automations, so in the standalone starter it stays hidden.

function.name: handToExternal
function.summary: Hands the whole shared Message over to the automation waiting on the other side.
function.accepts: The normalized message (text · title · at · source, optional lat/lng) of the success branch.
function.returns: handover — the Message object, handed to another automation.

nodes.name: Public Page output
nodes.description: A page on the automation own website.

info.aiSummary: Publishes the captured message to the public page feed: a row in the public-page table (date · source · title · text), read through api/rows?table=public-page. The node delivers the feed's DATA; how to render it is the page component's choice.

function.name: deliverPublicPage
function.summary: Appends the message to the public page feed table so the page can show it.
function.accepts: The normalized message (text · title · at · source) carried by the success branch.
function.returns: publicPageRowId — the id of the feed row written.

nodes.name: Calendar output
nodes.description: An event on the automation calendar.

info.aiSummary: Places the captured message as a calendar event. The event time is ctx.when (parsed by parseDate) when present, else the capture moment; ctx.needsWhen (no date found) is an honest ten-language "when?" refusal — no row is created. To make an occurrence actually deliver, it sets an ACTIVE integration on the SOURCE telegram channel (asked in Telegram → reminded in Telegram); api/calendar-tick then delivers it (step 307.6).

function.name: deliverCalendar
function.summary: Creates a calendar event titled like the message at its capture moment.
function.accepts: The captured message; optionally ctx.when (parsed date from parseDate) and ctx.needsWhen.
function.returns: calendarRowId and calendarWhen (ISO); refuses in ten languages when needsWhen is set.

nodes.name: Analytics output
nodes.description: A chart in the automation analytics.

info.aiSummary: Keeps per-channel counters of captured messages: one analytics-table row per input channel (metric "captured" · source · count · lastAt); every successful run increments its channel's counter through the journal store (the edit history keeps itself).

function.name: deliverAnalytics
function.summary: Increments the captured-messages counter of the run's input channel in the analytics table.
function.accepts: The normalized message (text · title · at · source) carried by the success branch.
function.returns: analyticsCount — the channel's counter value after this run.

nodes.name: Map output
nodes.description: A marker on the automation map.

info.aiSummary: Puts a marker on the automation map: a row in the map table (date · title · source · lat · lng). Coordinates are optional in the contract, so a message without lat/lng is delivered honestly-degraded — a skip with the reason in the run context, never an invented point.

function.name: deliverMap
function.summary: Writes a map marker at the message's lat/lng; without coordinates it skips honestly with a reason.
function.accepts: The normalized message; lat/lng when the input channel captured them.
function.returns: mapDelivery — "marker <id> at lat,lng" or "skipped: …" naming the missing coordinates.

nodes.name: Email output
nodes.description: An email the automation sends out.

info.aiSummary: Sends the captured message as an email via the shared transport (_lib/transport.ts, Resend). Recipient by explicitness: emailTo from the flow → the inbound sender (an honest reply) → RESEND_TO_EMAIL. An unconfigured channel (no key / no recipient) skips honestly with the reason; a refusal from the service with live keys throws.

envKeys.name: RESEND_API_KEY
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

envKeys.name: RESEND_FROM_EMAIL
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

envKeys.name: RESEND_TO_EMAIL
envKeys.comment: Optional owner address for fan-out letters; without it and without emailTo/emailFrom in the flow the node skips honestly.

function.name: deliverEmail
function.summary: Emails the message via Resend; unconfigured channel skips honestly, a service refusal throws.
function.accepts: The normalized message plus an optional recipient (emailTo, or emailFrom of an inbound letter).
function.returns: emailDelivery — "sent <id> to <address>" or "skipped: …" naming what is not configured.

nodes.name: Telegram Bot output
nodes.description: A message sent through the automation own Telegram bot.

info.aiSummary: Sends the captured message through the automation's own Telegram bot into its working chat (TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_CHAT_ID) via the shared transport. Unconfigured channel (no token/chat) skips honestly with the reason; a Telegram refusal with live keys throws.

envKeys.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

envKeys.name: TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_CHAT_ID
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

function.name: deliverTelegramBot
function.summary: Sends the message through the automation's bot; unconfigured channel skips honestly, a refusal throws.
function.accepts: The normalized message (text · title · at · source) carried by the success branch.
function.returns: telegramBotDelivery — "sent <message id>" or "skipped: …" naming the missing key.

nodes.name: User Telegram Chat output
nodes.description: A message written into the user own Telegram chat.

info.aiSummary: Writes the captured message into the USER'S personal Telegram chat (linked via api/telegram/link → TELEGRAM_USER_CHAT_ID; a chat id carried by the run itself wins — an honest reply to the sender). Same bot token as the bot channel: one service, one key. Unconfigured → honest skip; a refusal with live keys throws.

envKeys.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

envKeys.name: TELEGRAM_USER_CHAT_ID
envKeys.comment: The user's personal chat, linked natively via api/telegram/link (step 296); a run's own telegramChatId wins over it.

function.name: deliverUserTelegramChat
function.summary: Writes the message into the user's linked personal chat; unconfigured channel skips honestly.
function.accepts: The normalized message plus an optional telegramChatId carried by the run.
function.returns: userTelegramDelivery — "sent <id> to <chat>" or "skipped: …" naming what is missing.

nodes.name: Vector memory output
nodes.description: Output to the agent vector memory (LightRAG).

info.aiSummary: Remembers the captured message as a FACT: ingests it into LightRAG (folder-own call _lib/memory.ts, provenance projects/other/starter-v3?channel=<source>&record=<unique> — the unique tail is the uniqueness law) and writes a visible row into the vector-memory table (name · content · trackId). Service unreachable → honest skip; service refusal → throw.

envKeys.name: LIGHTRAG_URL
envKeys.comment: Optional — the node defaults to http://127.0.0.1:9621 (the platform memory service); an unreachable service degrades to an honest skip.

envKeys.name: LIGHTRAG_API_KEY
envKeys.comment: Optional — sent as X-API-Key when the memory service requires one for writes.

function.name: deliverVectorMemory
function.summary: Ingests the message into LightRAG with unique provenance and records the fact row; unreachable service skips honestly.
function.accepts: The normalized message (text · title · at · source) carried by the success branch.
function.returns: vectorMemoryDelivery ("remembered <track id>" or "skipped: …") and vectorRowId of the fact row.

nodes.name: Database output
nodes.description: If you activate this node, you can store and retrieve data in your own local database. If you also use object storage or a vector database, the local database keeps the links that locate those objects, too.

info.aiSummary: Writes the captured message as a record of the automation's own local database: a database-table row (name · text · source · date · storageIds · vectorIds). By the stores law the record HOLDS LINKS to the neighbouring stores: the vector fact's row id lands in vectorIds when the memory output ran earlier in the same fan-out.

function.name: deliverDatabase
function.summary: Writes a database record of the message, linking the vector fact written earlier in the same run.
function.accepts: The normalized message plus vectorRowId when the vector-memory output already ran.
function.returns: databaseRowId — the id of the database record written.

nodes.name: Storage output
nodes.description: If you activate this node, you can save and use media files and documents related to this automation in your own local storage.

info.aiSummary: Saves the captured message as a .txt FILE in the folder's object storage (_lib/store.ts → _data/runtime/objects/) and writes the storage-table row holding the link (fileKey · name · kind "text" · size) — bytes live in the store, the row holds the reference: the database→storage link of the stores law.

function.name: deliverStorage
function.summary: Saves the message as a .txt object and records the storage row holding its fileKey link.
function.accepts: The normalized message (text · title · at · source) carried by the success branch.
function.returns: storageFileKey and storageRowId — the object's key and the row that links to it.

nodes.name: Refusal
nodes.description: A request that must not be answered at all — server secrets, keys, passwords. Stands first so a refusal happens before any store or tool is touched.

info.aiSummary: A request that must not be answered at all — server secrets, keys, passwords. Stands first so a refusal happens before any store or tool is touched. Self-gates: claims the run only when the request is its own, otherwise returns null — an orderly stop of this branch. Writes intentClass/intentRoute into the context so the run journal shows why the run went where it went.

function.name: intentRefuse
function.summary: Recognizes a request for a secret and refuses it outright, without touching a store or a tool.
function.accepts: The captured Message text put into the context by the input node of the run channel.
function.returns: intentClass · intentRoute (+ the fields its route needs) — or null when the request belongs to another class.

outcomes.name: claimed
outcomes.when: this request belongs to this class
outcomes.puts: intentClass · intentRoute plus whatever the route needs

outcomes.name: passed
outcomes.when: the request belongs to another class
outcomes.puts: nothing: the flow reaches the next class untouched

nodes.name: Continuation
nodes.description: Not a new request but the second half of a previous one: a question is outstanding and this message answers it.

info.aiSummary: Not a new request but the second half of a previous one: a question is outstanding and this message answers it. Self-gates: claims the run only when the request is its own, otherwise returns null — an orderly stop of this branch. Writes intentClass/intentRoute into the context so the run journal shows why the run went where it went.

function.name: intentContinuation
function.summary: Detects that a question is outstanding and hands this message on as its answer.
function.accepts: The captured Message text put into the context by the input node of the run channel.
function.returns: intentClass · intentRoute (+ the fields its route needs) — or null when the request belongs to another class.

outcomes.name: claimed
outcomes.when: this request belongs to this class
outcomes.puts: intentClass · intentRoute plus whatever the route needs

outcomes.name: passed
outcomes.when: the request belongs to another class
outcomes.puts: nothing: the flow reaches the next class untouched

nodes.name: Self-description
nodes.description: A request about the automation itself — the answer is already in the passport, no store is involved.

info.aiSummary: A request about the automation itself — the answer is already in the passport, no store is involved. Self-gates: claims the run only when the request is its own, otherwise returns null — an orderly stop of this branch. Writes intentClass/intentRoute into the context so the run journal shows why the run went where it went.

function.name: intentSelfDescribe
function.summary: Recognizes a question about the automation itself and answers it from the passport.
function.accepts: The captured Message text put into the context by the input node of the run channel.
function.returns: intentClass · intentRoute (+ the fields its route needs) — or null when the request belongs to another class.

outcomes.name: claimed
outcomes.when: this request belongs to this class
outcomes.puts: intentClass · intentRoute plus whatever the route needs

outcomes.name: passed
outcomes.when: the request belongs to another class
outcomes.puts: nothing: the flow reaches the next class untouched

nodes.name: Control
nodes.description: The owner changes how the automation is BUILT — what it collects, what it asks, when it stays silent.

info.aiSummary: The owner changes how the automation is BUILT — what it collects, what it asks, when it stays silent. Self-gates: claims the run only when the request is its own, otherwise returns null — an orderly stop of this branch. Writes intentClass/intentRoute into the context so the run journal shows why the run went where it went.

function.name: intentControl
function.summary: Recognizes a request that changes the automation itself rather than its data.
function.accepts: The captured Message text put into the context by the input node of the run channel.
function.returns: intentClass · intentRoute (+ the fields its route needs) — or null when the request belongs to another class.

outcomes.name: claimed
outcomes.when: this request belongs to this class
outcomes.puts: intentClass · intentRoute plus whatever the route needs

outcomes.name: passed
outcomes.when: the request belongs to another class
outcomes.puts: nothing: the flow reaches the next class untouched

nodes.name: Composite
nodes.description: A request that needs two ordered actions: fetch from outside, then compare with what is kept.

info.aiSummary: A request that needs two ordered actions: fetch from outside, then compare with what is kept. Self-gates: claims the run only when the request is its own, otherwise returns null — an orderly stop of this branch. Writes intentClass/intentRoute into the context so the run journal shows why the run went where it went.

function.name: intentComposite
function.summary: Recognizes a two-step request and hands the middle an explicit plan.
function.accepts: The captured Message text put into the context by the input node of the run channel.
function.returns: intentClass · intentRoute (+ the fields its route needs) — or null when the request belongs to another class.

outcomes.name: claimed
outcomes.when: this request belongs to this class
outcomes.puts: intentClass · intentRoute plus whatever the route needs

outcomes.name: passed
outcomes.when: the request belongs to another class
outcomes.puts: nothing: the flow reaches the next class untouched

nodes.name: Fetch from outside
nodes.description: The data is NOT in the message — the named subject must be fetched from the outside world.

info.aiSummary: The data is NOT in the message — the named subject must be fetched from the outside world. Self-gates: claims the run only when the request is its own, otherwise returns null — an orderly stop of this branch. Writes intentClass/intentRoute into the context so the run journal shows why the run went where it went.

function.name: intentFetchExternal
function.summary: Recognizes a request to fetch a named subject from outside and passes the subject on.
function.accepts: The captured Message text put into the context by the input node of the run channel.
function.returns: intentClass · intentRoute (+ the fields its route needs) — or null when the request belongs to another class.

outcomes.name: claimed
outcomes.when: this request belongs to this class
outcomes.puts: intentClass · intentRoute plus whatever the route needs

outcomes.name: passed
outcomes.when: the request belongs to another class
outcomes.puts: nothing: the flow reaches the next class untouched

nodes.name: Read own

data.instruction: Ты — личный ассистент заметок в Telegram. Твоя роль: помогать владельцу быстро сохранять и находить информацию прямо в переписке. Ты умеешь: 📝 запоминать факты и заметки; ⏰ ставить напоминания по дате/времени и присылать их в срок; 🔎 находить сохранённое по вопросу; 💰 учитывать траты и доходы (в том числе по фото чека — распознаёшь сумму и категорию); 📍 отмечать места на карте. Стиль: тёплый, краткий, по делу, одно короткое сообщение, уместный эмодзи. Не пересказывай вопрос пользователя ему же. Если спрашивают, кто ты или зачем нужен — коротко и дружелюбно объясни, кто ты и что умеешь. На приветствие — поздоровайся и предложи помощь. Отвечай на языке пользователя.

cases.title: Ask the automation where it is published
cases.text: The owner asks the automation about ITSELF — «what page do you have?» — and gets the address of its public page straight back, without any store, any external tool and any key. If no address has been assigned yet, the automation says so plainly instead of inventing a link.
